title: One-Pan Chicken Thighs with Olives and Tomatoes
description: Crispy-skinned chicken thighs braised with burst cherry tomatoes, briny olives, and capers. Everything cooks in one pan — the chicken skin renders into the sauce, and the result is better than it has any right to be.

steps.text: Heat oven to 400°F. Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Cook without moving until the skin is deeply golden and releases easily from the pan, about 7 minutes.
Flip and sear the other side for 2 minutes, then transfer chicken to a plate.
Pour off all but about 1 tablespoon of fat from the pan. Add garlic and cook over medium heat until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the white wine and scrape up any browned bits stuck to the bottom — that's flavor. Let it simmer until reduced by roughly half, about 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes, olives, capers, oregano, and red pepper flakes. Stir to combine. Nestle the chicken thighs back in, skin-side up, so the skin stays above the liquid.
Transfer the skillet to the oven. Roast until the chicken reaches 165°F and the tomatoes have burst into a saucy mess, about 20 minutes.
Scatter torn basil over the top. Serve straight from the pan with crusty bread to soak up the juices.
